gen-megrim-gf-georama: Angular and futuristic, Megrim builds its o as a ring with a constant wall, while Georama keeps things approachable. Georama's barely rising capitals leave the heading all the room it wants.
gen-megrim-gf-heebo: Pipe-cleaner strokes of one measured thickness give Megrim its angular, futuristic look. Heebo follows with a tall central band of text and curves that stop short, so paragraphs move along steadily.
gen-megrim-gf-hind-vadodara: Megrim's c opens as wide as a bent paperclip, every stroke ending at one measured thickness. And where Megrim is built for display, Hind Vadodara handles the text with spacious terminal gaps and tall bowls.
gen-megrim-gf-krub: Sharp and sci-fi, Megrim has bold letters with no thick or thin parts. Krub sits beneath in sans-serif, its open-ended curves and pronounced x-height giving the text a contemporary ease against the heading's angles.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend: Megrim is angular and futuristic, with every stroke ending at one measured thickness and a skyward x-height line. Lexend's outsized lowercase and open jaws supply a warm, approachable counterweight.
gen-megrim-gf-liter: Liter is a modern sans-serif with no stroke contrast, great vertical presence and wide mouths on round forms. Under Megrim's angular heading, long paragraphs would settle into a smooth, professional hum.
gen-megrim-gf-mada: Mada is approachable and modern, its curves refusing to close and its midzone towering. Mada then takes the text beside Megrim, whose letters have no thick or thin parts, leaving angles above and openness below.
gen-megrim-gf-martel-sans: Angular and futuristic, Megrim's tubular, wire-like letters meet Martel Sans, with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line. Megrim earns its keep when it is big and short.
gen-megrim-gf-matangi: Megrim is angular and futuristic, its strokes ending at one measured thickness and its c as open as a bent paperclip. Matangi follows with twine-like strokes and a hefty lowercase to anchor it.
gen-megrim-gf-maven-pro: Futuristic and angular, Megrim hangs every stroke at one measured thickness, while Maven Pro keeps a welcoming gap in its c. Megrim excels at display; Maven Pro at running text.
